name: Desktop app installer
explanation: A setup package that installs your desktop app the normal way on each operating system, such as an MSI or MSIX on Windows, a DMG or pkg on macOS, or a deb, rpm or AppImage on Linux, and removes it cleanly later.
synonyms: setup package;msi installer;msix package;dmg disk image;nsis installer;deb and rpm packages;appimage
triggers: make an installer;setup exe for my app;package my app for mac;uninstall cleanly;distribute my desktop app;installer wizard;linux package for my app;install program on windows
requirements: Produce the native package format users expect on each OS you support;Sign the installer and every binary inside it to avoid unknown-publisher warnings;Upgrade in place over an older version without losing user settings or data;Make uninstall remove program files, shortcuts and registrations, and ask before deleting user data;Choose per-user or per-machine install on purpose, since per-machine installs need admin rights;Keep a stable product identity (upgrade code, bundle id, package name) across all versions;Build the installers in CI for every target OS and architecture
done_when: A clean machine can install and launch the app without unsigned or unknown-publisher warnings;Installing a new version over an old one keeps settings and data;Uninstalling leaves no shortcuts, menu entries or file associations behind;Installers exist for every supported OS and architecture

name: Desktop auto-update
explanation: Letting an installed desktop app find, download, check and install its own new versions, so users stay up to date without downloading an installer again.
synonyms: in-app updater;self-updating app;update manifest;update channel;differential updates;background updates
triggers: app updates itself;check for updates button;restart to update;update without reinstalling;keep users on the latest version;download update in the background;beta updates for testers
requirements: Serve updates over HTTPS and verify the update's signature before installing it;Check and download in the background, and install on restart or when the user agrees;Offer stable and beta channels and roll a release out gradually;Retry failed or partial downloads and keep the current version working meanwhile;Let admins disable or defer updates in managed environments;Refuse downgrades unless allowed, and keep a way to ship a fix if an update breaks startup;Show the new version number and what changed
done_when: An installed old version finds, downloads and applies the new one;A tampered or unsigned update is rejected;Cutting the download halfway leaves the app working on the old version;Beta users get beta builds and stable users do not

name: macOS notarization and hardened runtime
explanation: Apple's automated malware check for Mac apps distributed outside the App Store: you sign the app, upload it to Apple's notary service and attach the result, so Gatekeeper lets users open it without a warning.
synonyms: notarization;notarytool;hardened runtime;gatekeeper;stapling;notarization ticket;developer id signing
triggers: app is damaged and cannot be opened;developer cannot be verified;mac blocks my app;unidentified developer warning;distribute mac app outside the store;apple malware check
requirements: Sign every executable and nested framework with a Developer ID Application certificate and a secure timestamp;Enable the hardened runtime and add only the runtime exceptions the app really needs;Submit with notarytool, since the old altool route is no longer accepted, and read the log when it fails;Staple the ticket to the app, DMG or pkg so Gatekeeper can check it offline;Notarize every build you ship, including updates and bundled helper tools;Automate signing and notarization in CI with the API key kept as a secret
done_when: spctl assessment accepts the app as a notarized Developer ID app;A downloaded copy opens on a clean Mac without a Gatekeeper warning;stapler validate succeeds on the shipped file

name: macOS App Sandbox and entitlements
explanation: A macOS security mode that keeps an app inside its own container folder and lets it use files, network or devices only if it declares them, so a bug or attack cannot reach the rest of the system. The Mac App Store requires it.
synonyms: app sandbox;sandbox entitlements;entitlements plist;security-scoped bookmarks;app container
triggers: mac app cannot read files;app store says i need sandbox;access folders from a mac app;limit what my mac app can access;sandboxed app cannot connect
requirements: Enable the app sandbox entitlement and add only the entitlements the app actually uses;Get file access through the open and save panels and keep it with security-scoped bookmarks;Expect data in the app container and migrate data from older unsandboxed versions;Sign helper tools with the sandbox and inherit entitlements;Declare network client or server entitlements before making or accepting connections;Test the signed sandboxed release build, not only a debug run
done_when: The signed app shows the sandbox entitlement and no unused ones;Files the user opened are still accessible after relaunch;Every feature works in the signed sandboxed build

name: Publishing to Mac App Store / Microsoft Store
explanation: Packaging a desktop app and submitting it to the Mac App Store or Microsoft Store, meeting their sandbox, signing and review rules so it can be found and installed there.
synonyms: mac app store submission;microsoft store submission;store package;store listing;app review
triggers: put my app in the microsoft store;sell my desktop app in a store;submit mac app for review;app rejected by mac app store;windows store listing
requirements: Sign with the store's distribution certificate, or let the store sign the package, as each store requires;Enable App Sandbox for the Mac App Store, and submit MSIX or an MSI or EXE that meets Microsoft Store policies;Remove your own updater from Mac App Store and MSIX builds so the store delivers updates;Use the store's in-app purchase where its rules require it for digital goods;Provide privacy details, age rating, screenshots and a privacy policy link;Test the exact store package on a clean machine before submitting
done_when: The store build passes the store's validation checks;Mac App Store and MSIX installs update through the store, not the app's own updater;The listing is approved and installs on a clean machine

name: Enterprise deployment and managed settings
explanation: Making a desktop app easy for company IT teams to install on many computers without prompts and to configure centrally with policies, such as fixing the server address or turning off updates.
synonyms: silent install;unattended install;per-machine install;group policy;admx template;managed preferences;mdm configuration profile
triggers: install on all company computers;install without any prompts;lock settings for employees;it admin rollout;deploy through device management;company wide install
requirements: Support silent install and uninstall with documented command-line options and exit codes;Offer a per-machine install that does not need each user to be an admin;Read settings from group policy or MDM profiles and let them override user choices;Show users which settings are managed and disable those controls;Let admins control auto-update and telemetry;Publish a policy template or settings schema and the list of network endpoints for firewalls
done_when: A silent command-line install succeeds with exit code 0 and no prompts;A setting pushed by policy is applied and users cannot change it;Uninstalling through management tools removes the app cleanly

name: Multi-architecture builds (Apple silicon and ARM64)
explanation: Building the app for each kind of processor, such as Intel and ARM, or as one universal file that contains both, so it runs at full speed on every supported computer.
synonyms: universal binary;apple silicon support;arm64 build;fat binary;multi-arch build;windows on arm
triggers: app slow on m1 mac;runs under rosetta;build for arm laptops;support apple silicon and intel;native arm version
requirements: Build every native module, helper and bundled binary for each architecture, not only the main executable;On macOS ship one universal binary or separate arm64 and x64 downloads;Serve the matching download and update file for each architecture;Test on real hardware for each architecture, not only under emulation;Check that third-party native libraries support ARM64 before relying on them;Confirm the architectures inside shipped binaries with tools such as lipo or file
done_when: The app runs natively, not emulated, on ARM machines;Every binary in the bundle contains the expected architectures;Auto-update delivers the build that matches each machine

name: System tray / menu bar icon
explanation: A small icon for your app in the Windows notification area near the clock or the macOS menu bar, with a menu, so the app can keep running in the background and be reached quickly.
synonyms: tray icon;notification area icon;menu bar extra;status item;tray menu
triggers: icon near the clock;app icon in the top bar on mac;minimize to tray;keep running when window is closed;run in background with an icon;small icon at top of mac screen
requirements: Use a template (monochrome) image on macOS and sizes that suit light and dark taskbars;Give the icon a tooltip and a menu with at least Open and Quit;Hide to the tray on window close only if users can tell the app is still running;Tray support differs between Linux desktops, so keep another way to reach the app;Show status by changing the icon or tooltip, not by opening windows;Remove the icon on quit so no ghost icon remains
done_when: The icon is sharp in light and dark themes and on high-DPI screens;Quit in the tray menu fully exits the app;The app is still reachable on a system without a tray

name: Custom title bar (frameless window)
explanation: Replacing the operating system's window frame with your own title bar design, while keeping dragging, resizing and the minimize, maximize and close buttons working like a normal window.
synonyms: frameless window;client-side decorations;custom window chrome;draggable region;titlebar overlay
triggers: remove the window frame;make my own title bar;window cannot be dragged;hide title bar but keep buttons;tabs in the title bar
requirements: Mark drag regions explicitly and exclude buttons and inputs inside them;Keep native window controls or a title bar overlay where the platform supports it;Keep snap layouts on the Windows 11 maximize button and the macOS window buttons in their usual place;Keep double-click to maximize, the system window menu and resizing from the edges;Show active and inactive states and follow dark mode and high contrast;Make window controls reachable by keyboard and named for screen readers
done_when: The window can be dragged, resized, snapped and maximized like a native one;Hovering maximize on Windows 11 shows snap layouts;Window controls work with the keyboard and a screen reader

name: File type associations
explanation: Registering your app as the program for its file types, so double-clicking such a file opens it in your app and the file shows your icon.
synonyms: file association;file extension handler;open with menu;document types;uniform type identifier;progid
triggers: double click file opens my app;register my file extension;custom icon for my files;set as default app for a file type;my app in the open with list
requirements: Declare associations in the installer or app manifest instead of writing registry keys at runtime;Use your own extension and type id, and do not force yourself as default: Windows makes the user choose;Provide a document icon for each file type;Handle files passed at launch and while already running, including several at once;Remove associations on uninstall;Check the opened file's content and show a clear error for damaged or wrong files
done_when: Double-clicking a file of the type opens it in the app;Opening a file while the app runs reuses the running app;The app is listed in Open with and the files show its icon

name: Custom URL protocol handler
explanation: Registering your own link prefix such as myapp:// so that clicking such a link in a browser or another app opens your desktop app at the right place.
synonyms: custom protocol handler;protocol registration;url protocol handler;app protocol link
triggers: link in browser opens my desktop app;link that opens my app;login in browser then return to the app;open desktop app from a website
requirements: Register the protocol at install time and handle it whether the app is running or not;Treat every incoming URL as untrusted and accept only known routes and parameters;Never run commands, open files or load remote pages straight from URL parameters;Use a state value and PKCE when the link completes a browser login;Pick a protocol name unlikely to clash, such as one based on your domain;Forward links from a second launch to the running instance
done_when: Clicking a link opens the app at the right screen, running or not;Malformed or unknown URLs are rejected without side effects;A browser login returns to the app and matches the original request

name: Single instance app
explanation: Making sure only one copy of the app runs at a time, so opening it again brings the existing window forward and passes along any file or link instead of starting a duplicate.
synonyms: single instance lock;instance mutex;second instance handling
triggers: app opens twice;prevent two copies running;focus the existing window;only one copy of my app
requirements: Take the lock early at startup and exit the second instance quickly;Pass the second launch's arguments, files and URLs to the first instance;Bring the existing window to the front, restoring it if minimized or hidden in the tray;Scope the lock per user so other users on the same machine are not blocked;Make sure a crash releases the lock so the app can start again
done_when: Launching the app again focuses the existing window;Opening a file while running opens it in the existing instance;After a crash the app starts normally

name: Drag and drop files with the OS
explanation: Letting users drag files from the desktop or file manager into your app, and drag items out of your app into folders or other programs.
synonyms: native file drag and drop;file drop target;drag out to desktop;external drag and drop
triggers: drag a file from the desktop into my app;drop files on the window;drag an item out to a folder;drag image into explorer
requirements: Show a clear drop area and accept only supported types, with a message for the rest;Handle several files and folders at once, and large files without freezing the interface;Validate dropped paths and file contents before reading them;When dragging out, give the file a sensible name and create it in the target location;In web-based UIs, stop the window from navigating to a file dropped outside the drop area;Keep an Open button as the keyboard alternative;Do not run the app as admin: Windows blocks drops from Explorer into elevated windows
done_when: Dropping supported files imports them and other files show a message;Dropping a file anywhere in the window never replaces the app's page;Dragging an item out creates the file in the target folder

name: Document open, save and unsaved changes
explanation: The usual way desktop apps handle documents: New, Open, Save and Save As, a mark when there are unsaved changes, and a prompt before closing or quitting so no work is lost.
synonyms: document-based app;save as;dirty document state;edited indicator;new open save
triggers: save and save as;ask to save before closing;dot on close button when unsaved;untitled document;file menu save
requirements: Show the file name in the title and an edited mark when there are unsaved changes;Ask to save, discard or cancel when closing a window or quitting with unsaved work;Save to a temporary file and then replace the original so a crash cannot corrupt it;Use the platform shortcuts for New, Open, Save and Save As;Handle read-only files, missing folders and full disks with clear errors;Default Save As to the last folder, the current name and the right extension
done_when: Closing with unsaved changes always asks first;A crash during save leaves the previous file intact;The edited mark clears after saving

name: Recent documents list
explanation: Keeping a list of files the user opened recently and showing it in the app's menu, the macOS Dock menu and the Windows taskbar jump list for quick reopening.
synonyms: recent files;most recently used list;open recent;mru list
triggers: list of recently opened files;open recent menu;recent files on the dock icon;reopen the last file
requirements: Add files to the OS recent list when opened or saved so the Dock and jump list stay in sync;On Windows register the file type first or recent items will not show in the jump list;Remove or disable entries for files that no longer exist;Limit the list length and offer Clear Recent;Store entries so they survive restarts, using security-scoped bookmarks in sandboxed Mac apps
done_when: Recently opened files show in the app menu, Dock menu and jump list;Choosing an entry opens the file or says it is missing;Clear Recent empties the list

name: Detecting external file changes
explanation: Noticing when a file or folder the app has open is changed, renamed or deleted by another program, and reloading or warning the user instead of silently overwriting it.
synonyms: file watcher;file system watcher;file change notifications;reload on change
triggers: file changed on disk;another program edited my file;reload when the file changes;warn before overwriting a newer file;open file was deleted or moved
requirements: Debounce bursts of events, since one save can fire several change events;Compare modification time, size or a hash before saving to avoid overwriting newer content;Reload quietly if there are no local edits, otherwise ask whether to reload or keep the user's version;Handle renames, deletes and network drives where events may be missing;Stop watching closed files so the app does not run out of watch handles;Fall back to polling where native watching is unreliable
done_when: Editing the open file elsewhere updates or warns in the app;Saving never silently overwrites a newer version on disk;Deleting the file shows a clear notice

name: Multiple windows
explanation: Letting a desktop app open several windows, such as one per document or separate settings and tool windows, and keeping them in sync and behaving correctly together.
synonyms: multi-window app;child window;secondary window;document windows;owned window
triggers: open in a new window;separate settings window;several documents side by side;tear off a panel into a window;second window in desktop app
requirements: Decide which windows are modal, owned by a parent or independent;Keep data in sync between windows through one source of truth;Follow platform conventions: on macOS the app usually stays open after its last window closes;Focus the existing settings or about window instead of opening a duplicate;Release listeners and resources when a window closes;Give each window a clear title and list open windows in the Window menu
done_when: Changes in one window appear in the others;Closing windows frees memory and leaves no hidden processes;A modal dialog blocks only the window it belongs to

name: Remembering window size and position
explanation: Saving each window's size, position and maximized state when it closes and restoring it next time, while making sure it never reopens off-screen.
synonyms: window state restore;saved window bounds;remember window position
triggers: remember window size;app opens in the same place;window opens off screen;restore maximized window
requirements: Save size, position, maximized and fullscreen state when the window moves or closes;Keep the normal size separately from the maximized state;Check the saved position against the current displays and move the window on-screen if needed;Clamp the size to the display's usable area;Account for different scaling between monitors when saving and restoring
done_when: The app reopens where it was left;After unplugging the second monitor the window opens on the main screen;A maximized window reopens maximized and restores to its old size

name: High-DPI and multi-monitor scaling
explanation: Making a desktop app look sharp at any display scaling, such as 150 or 200 percent, and keep the right size when a window moves between monitors with different settings.
synonyms: dpi awareness;per-monitor dpi;display scaling;retina support;device pixel ratio
triggers: app looks blurry on 4k screen;text fuzzy on my laptop;wrong size on other monitor;150 percent scaling
requirements: Declare per-monitor (v2) DPI awareness in the app manifest on Windows;Handle DPI change events and rescale layout and images when a window moves between monitors;Provide images at 1x, 2x and higher, or use vector icons;Convert consistently between physical and logical pixels for window sizes and mouse positions;Test at 100, 150 and 200 percent and with mixed-scaling monitors
done_when: Text and icons are sharp at 200 percent scaling;Moving a window to a monitor with different scaling keeps its size right;Clicks land where things are drawn at every scale

name: Taskbar and Dock integration
explanation: Using the Windows taskbar and the macOS Dock to show progress, unread counts and attention requests on the app icon, and to add quick actions to its right-click menu.
synonyms: taskbar progress;dock badge;jump list;thumbnail toolbar;dock menu;overlay icon
triggers: progress bar on taskbar icon;number on the dock icon;flash taskbar for attention;bounce the dock icon;right click taskbar menu
requirements: Show progress for long tasks and clear it when done or failed;Use badges or overlay icons for counts and clear them when items are read;Request attention sparingly and only when the window is not focused;On Windows set an AppUserModelID so taskbar features attach to the right app;Keep jump list and Dock menu items short and pointing to real actions;Do not rely on these alone, since users may hide the taskbar or Dock
done_when: A long task shows progress on the icon and clears at the end;The badge count matches unread items;Jump list and Dock menu items open the right action

name: Desktop OS notifications
explanation: Showing the operating system's own pop-up notifications from a desktop app, so users see important events even when the app is in the background.
synonyms: native os notifications;windows toast notifications;macos user notifications;action center notification
triggers: popup in the corner of the screen;notify user when app is minimized;notification with a reply button;click notification opens the window
requirements: Check notification permission and handle it being turned off;On Windows set an AppUserModelID with a Start menu shortcut, or notifications may not appear;Make clicking a notification open the matching window and item;Respect Focus and Do Not Disturb, and do not flood users with missed notifications later;Let users turn notification types off in the app;Keep sensitive content out of notification text
done_when: Notifications appear from an installed build on each supported OS;Clicking one opens the right content;Turning a type off in settings stops it

name: Global keyboard shortcuts
explanation: Key combinations that trigger your app from anywhere, even when another program is in front, such as a shortcut that opens a quick search window.
synonyms: global hotkey;system-wide shortcut;global accelerator
triggers: shortcut works when app is not focused;press keys anywhere to open my app;quick launcher key combo;push to talk key
requirements: Check that registration succeeded, since another app may already own the combination;Let users change or turn off each global shortcut;Unregister shortcuts when the app quits or the feature is turned off;Avoid combinations the OS reserves;Explain and request accessibility permission on macOS only when a shortcut needs it;Some Linux Wayland sessions block global shortcuts, so offer a fallback

name: Start at login
explanation: Letting users choose to start the app automatically when they sign in to the computer, optionally hidden in the tray, using each operating system's supported method.

triggers: open my app when computer starts;start automatically on boot;launch when i sign in;start minimized at login
requirements: Make it opt-in or clearly visible, with a setting to turn it off;Use the supported mechanism: login items on macOS, the Run key or a startup task on Windows, XDG autostart on Linux;Pass a flag so a login launch can start hidden in the tray;Keep the setting in sync with the OS, since users can disable it there;Remove the entry on uninstall;Keep startup work light so it does not slow down sign-in

name: Background service (Windows service, launchd daemon)
explanation: A helper program that the operating system starts at boot or sign-in and keeps running in the background, restarting it if it crashes, such as a sync engine or a privileged helper.
synonyms: windows service;launchd daemon;launch agent;systemd service;system daemon
triggers: run something when no one is logged in;keep a process running after reboot;helper that runs as admin;restart process if it crashes

done_when: The service starts on boot and restarts after being killed;It runs under a limited account;Uninstalling stops and removes it

name: Bundling a helper executable (sidecar)
explanation: Shipping a separate program, such as a command-line tool or local server, inside your desktop app and starting it from the app when needed.
synonyms: sidecar binary;bundled cli tool;helper process;child process;utility process
triggers: ship a binary with my app;run a python server inside my desktop app;start a local server from the app;call a command line tool from the app
requirements: Build and bundle the helper for every OS and architecture under the expected file name;Sign and notarize the helper together with the app;Allow only fixed commands and validated arguments, never pass raw user input to a shell;Stop the helper when the app quits or crashes so no orphan processes remain;Bind a local server to localhost on a random port and require a token;Detect the helper crashing and report or restart it

name: App data and settings storage location
explanation: Saving a desktop app's settings, caches, logs and user files in the per-user folders each operating system provides, instead of next to the program itself.
synonyms: user data directory;appdata folder;application support folder;xdg base directories;roaming app data;per-user config directory
triggers: where to save settings;settings lost after update;cannot write to program files;config file location;where to put log files;cache folder for my app;app needs admin to save
requirements: Never write to the install folder, it may be read-only and is replaced on update;Ask the OS or framework for each folder path instead of hard-coding drive letters or home paths;Keep settings, caches, logs and documents in separate folders so caches can be cleared safely;On Windows use roaming app data only for small settings and local app data for caches and large files;On Linux follow the XDG variables and fall back to ~/.config, ~/.local/share and ~/.cache when unset;Put files the user created in Documents or a folder they chose, not hidden in app data;Version the settings format and migrate old files instead of crashing on them;Decide what the uninstaller removes and keep user documents
done_when: The app runs and saves settings as a standard user without admin rights;Settings survive an app update and reinstall;Deleting the cache folder loses no settings or user work;Each folder lands in the expected OS location on Windows, macOS and Linux

name: OS keychain credential storage
explanation: Keeping passwords, tokens and keys a desktop app needs in the operating system's protected credential store, so they are not readable from a plain file on disk.
synonyms: windows credential manager;dpapi;macos keychain services;libsecret;secret service api;os credential vault
triggers: keep me signed in desktop;save api token safely;store password on the computer;token in plain text file;where to keep refresh token;encrypt saved password
requirements: Store only secrets in the credential store and keep other settings in normal files;Check encryption is available before saving and do not silently fall back to plain text;On Linux detect when no secret service is running and tell the user instead of storing unprotected data;Never log, print or send secrets in crash reports;Store refresh tokens rather than passwords where the service supports OAuth;Delete stored secrets on sign-out and on uninstall when possible;Handle the store being locked, denied or reset by asking the user to sign in again
done_when: No password or token appears in plain text in any app file or log;Signing out removes the stored secret;A denied or missing keychain shows a clear prompt instead of crashing;Copying the app data folder to another account or machine does not expose the token

name: Web-view desktop app security (IPC isolation)
explanation: Locking down a desktop app built with web technology so a malicious page or script in its window cannot reach the computer's files, processes or native features.

done_when: A script in the page cannot call require or reach Node APIs;An IPC call with bad arguments or from an unexpected frame is rejected;Clicking an external link opens the system browser, not a new app window;The app passes the framework's security checklist with no exceptions left undocumented

name: Sleep prevention and suspend/resume handling
explanation: Keeping the computer or screen awake while a long task runs, and reacting correctly when the system sleeps, wakes, locks the screen or switches to battery.

triggers: stop computer going to sleep;keep screen on during download;app breaks after laptop wakes;detect laptop on battery;screen lock event;pause work when computer sleeps

done_when: The computer does not sleep during a long export and sleeps normally afterwards;After wake the app reconnects and shows fresh data without a restart;Locking the screen triggers the expected away or privacy behaviour;No sleep block remains active when the app is idle

name: Graceful quit and session restore
explanation: Saving work and closing cleanly when the user quits or the computer logs off, restarts or installs updates, then reopening the same windows and work on the next launch.

triggers: app loses work on restart;reopen windows where i left off;windows update closed my app;save before computer shuts down;restore tabs after crash;app blocks shutdown

done_when: Restarting the computer with unsaved work loses nothing;After relaunch the same windows and documents reopen;An update installer can close and restart the app without user action;A missing file from the last session is skipped with a short message

name: Printing from a desktop app

name: Kiosk mode
explanation: Locking a computer or device to run only one app full screen, so the public cannot leave it, open other programs or change settings, and it comes back by itself after a crash or reboot.

name: System proxy and corporate certificate support
explanation: Making a desktop app's network traffic use the computer's proxy settings and trusted company certificates, so it still connects on office and other managed networks.
